newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share price index soars on oil gains.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share price index soars on oil gains.

text.p: Solid price gains by oil marketers saw the Nigerian stock exchange all-share index rise sharply on Thursday, traders said.
The index rose to 6676.74 from 6654.48 on Tuesday.
The market was closed on Wednesday because of a public holiday in honour of Nigeria's first president Nnamdi Azikiwe, who died in May and will buried on Saturday.
One deal worth 1.9 million naira was recorded in the industrial loans/preference stock sector on Thursday.
Among the equities, leading banks, conglomerates, paints and chemical firms continued to decline as investors resumed offloading shares with Christmas expenses on their minds.
Union Bank and NAL Merchant Bank fell five kobo apiece to 6.65 naira and 5.10 naira, respectively while Guaranty Trust Bank dropped 20 kobo to 13.60 naira.
Lever Brothers slid by 15 kobo to 24.95 naira because more investors felt it would go lower in the weeks ahead.
CFAO, the Franco-Nigerian trading group, dropped five kobo to 3.80 naira. It has now shed 50 percent of its value, from its 7.68 naira highest price this year on poor performances, said traders.
Chemical and Allied Products was down by five kobo to 6.90 naira. Berger Paints was down by a similar margin at 5.05 naira.
Cadbury and Guinness dropped three kobo each at 6.55 naira and 25.67 naira, respectively.
But the fortunes of Nigerian Breweries continued to improve, appreciating 60 kobo to 12.60 naira as more investors jostled to increase their stake in the resurging giant.
It shared the top gainers spot with oil marketers Unipetrol and National Oil whose 60 kobo gains raised their prices to 48.60 naira and 40.00 naira, respectively.
Agip soared by 50 kobo on its improved mid-year result which saw after-tax profit to end-June jump to 97.9 million naira from 74.8 million naira in the first half of 1995.
